name: Punk Rock
about: Punk rock proper is the first wave: the New York bands around CBGB from 1974, the London explosion of 1976 and 1977, and the scenes that caught fire in Los Angeles, Belfast and Brisbane right behind them. The Ramones fixed the form, two-minute songs on downstroked barre chords at a tempo nobody had sustained before, and the Sex Pistols gave it a sneer and a scandal, while The Clash gave it politics and a wider range. The voice is shouted rather than sung, the production flat and loud, the lyrics about boredom, the dole and bad television. By 1980 the style had already split into hardcore, post-punk and pop punk, but the three-chord template survived every revival, from Rancid in the 1990s to Amyl and the Sniffers now.

artists.name: Sex Pistols
artists.why: one album, one scandal, year zero

artists.name: The Clash
artists.why: punk's political conscience and widest reach

artists.name: The Damned
artists.why: first UK punk single and album

artists.name: Buzzcocks
artists.why: Manchester's masters of the punk love song

artists.name: The Jam
artists.why: mod suits and Paul Weller's fury

artists.name: X-Ray Spex
artists.why: Poly Styrene, saxophone and day-glo rage

artists.name: Stiff Little Fingers
artists.why: Belfast punk from inside the Troubles

artists.name: Richard Hell & The Voidoids

artists.name: Rancid

albums.title: Horses
albums.why: John Cale produced the poet's debut, where Gloria and Land fused French symbolism with garage rock and opened the door for everything that followed at CBGB.

albums.title: Ramones
albums.why: Fourteen songs in twenty-nine minutes, recorded for six thousand dollars: the record that defined punk's speed, brevity and humor before the word stuck.

albums.title: Damned Damned Damned
albums.why: The first British punk album, slapdash and thrilling, with New Rose and Neat Neat Neat outrunning everything else on it.

albums.title: The Clash
albums.why: White Riot, Janie Jones and the Police and Thieves cover put politics, reggae and tower-block fury into British punk's most urgent debut.

albums.title: Rocket to Russia
albums.why: Sheena Is a Punk Rocker and Rockaway Beach made the third album the Ramones' most tuneful and best-produced, their bubblegum side at full strength.

albums.title: Blank Generation
albums.why: Robert Quine's splintered guitar and Hell's nervous poetry made the smartest record of the New York scene and gave the movement its catchphrase.

albums.title: Young, Loud and Snotty
albums.why: Stiv Bators's Iggy routine and Cheetah Chrome's riffs on Sonic Reducer brought Cleveland's nihilism to CBGB on the rawest American punk debut of 1977.

albums.title: L.A.M.F.
albums.why: Johnny Thunders's post-Dolls band cut Chinese Rocks and Born to Lose in London with a famously muddy mix, and the songs survive it.

albums.title: In the City
albums.why: Paul Weller was eighteen when the mod-revivalist trio cut this fast, sharp debut, closer to The Who than the Pistols and better played than either.

albums.title: (I'm) Stranded
albums.why: Recorded in Brisbane isolation before the band had heard the Ramones, the debut proved punk was arriving independently on three continents.

albums.title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols
albums.why: The one album the Pistols made, thick with Steve Jones's overdubbed guitars and Johnny Rotten's sneer, remains punk's most famous object.

albums.title: Pink Flag
albums.why: Twenty-one songs, some under a minute, that reduced punk to pure shape and foreshadowed post-punk, hardcore and Britpop alike.

albums.title: Another Music in a Different Kitchen
albums.why: Pete Shelley's debut album after Howard Devoto's exit set romantic anxiety to buzzsaw guitars and a surprising streak of Krautrock repetition.

albums.title: Germfree Adolescents
albums.why: Poly Styrene's day-glo consumer satire and Lora Logic's saxophone made the only British punk debut as original as the Pistols' and funnier.

albums.title: Crossing the Red Sea with The Adverts
albums.why: T.V. Smith's literate songs and Gaye Advert's bass on One Chord Wonders and Bored Teenagers made a debut most first-wave bands never matched.

albums.title: Generation X
albums.why: Billy Idol's pop instincts were already showing on Ready Steady Go and Your Generation, a glossy punk record the purists disowned and the charts liked.

albums.title: Inflammable Material
albums.why: Suspect Device and Alternative Ulster, written from inside the Troubles, made the first independent album to chart in Britain and Belfast's punk statement.

albums.title: The Undertones
albums.why: Teenage Kicks and a dozen songs about girls and chocolate, sung in Feargal Sharkey's quaver, made the most innocent and tuneful record of British punk.

albums.title: (GI)
albums.why: Joan Jett produced Darby Crash and Pat Smear's only album, the chaotic bridge between first-wave Los Angeles punk and the hardcore that followed.

albums.title: The Crack
albums.why: Babylon's Burning and the reggae-schooled rhythm section made the Ruts' only album with Malcolm Owen one of the tightest records of the second wave.

albums.title: London Calling
albums.why: A double album of punk, reggae, rockabilly and soul that outgrew the genre's limits without losing its purpose, and the decade's great rock record.

albums.title: ...And Out Come the Wolves
albums.why: Tim Armstrong and Lars Frederiksen's Clash devotion on Ruby Soho and Time Bomb made the 1990s' best straight punk rock record and sold a million copies.

albums.title: Joy as an Act of Resistance
albums.why: Joe Talbot's shouted sermons on toxic masculinity and immigration over post-punk guitars made the Bristol band Britain's most argued-about punk act.

albums.title: Comfort to Me
albums.why: Amy Taylor's Melbourne band played the 1977 pub-punk template harder and funnier than anyone in years, with Guided by Angels as the anthem.
